mainTopic: רבי יוחנן's rule אין למדין מן הכללות, with proofs from three משניות, and whether a water-and-salt mixture counts for עירוב and for מעשר שני.
overview: The amud opens with the last words of the משנה: רבי יהודה lets a כהן put his עירוב in a cemetery, because he can shield himself and go eat it. The גמרא then quotes רבי יוחנן: we do not learn from general statements in a משנה, even when the משנה lists exceptions with the word חוץ. From the word 'even', the גמרא concludes that his main case was the משנה in קידושין about מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, which says כל and has no חוץ. It shows that this rule has exceptions in both directions: מצה, שמחה and הקהל obligate women, while תלמוד תורה, פריה ורביה and פדיון הבן do not. אביי (or רבי ירמיה) proves the 'even with חוץ' part from a משנה about a זב, whose list leaves out the מרכב, the handle of a saddle. רבינא (or רב נחמן) brings a second proof from our own משנה, whose list of foods not allowed for an עירוב leaves out truffles and mushrooms. Next the גמרא discusses a teaching that water and salt mixed together are allowed. One אמורא says it is about עירוב and the other says it is about buying with מעשר שני money, which needs real produce. רבי יצחק taught the מעשר version, and a ברייתא about fish brine challenges him. רב יוסף begins to answer, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the משנה: why a כהן's עירוב can be placed in a cemetery
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with רבי יהודה's reason that a כהן's עירוב may be placed even in a בית הקברות. The כהן can shield himself, go there, and eat the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he can make a barrier, and go and eat.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of the משנה. רבי יהודה explains why a כהן's עירוב can be put even in a cemetery: the כהן is able to reach it and eat it without becoming טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב must be food the person could actually eat at that spot. A כהן normally may not enter a cemetery. רבי יהודה says this is not a problem, because the כהן can travel inside a closed box or carriage that blocks the טומאה, so the food is still reachable for him.

keyTerms.meaning: To make a barrier or separation (here, between himself and the טומאה of the graves)
Cemetery. This is the place under discussion; the term is not in this line itself.
Food placed to establish a person's שבת location (here עירובי תחומין)
Priest. He is forbidden to become impure from the dead.

steps.confusionAlert: Earlier in this same משנה it says 'בכל מערבין... חוץ מן המים ומן המלח' (we may make an עירוב with anything except water and salt). Keep that word חוץ in mind. It is the key to step 3.

phrases.english: because he is able to make a barrier,
phrases.notes: He shields himself from the grave-impurity, e.g., in a closed box or carriage.

phrases.english: and go and eat.
phrases.notes: The food is therefore 'available' to him, so the עירוב works.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a כהן's עירוב may be placed even in a cemetery, because he can reach and eat it without contracting טומאה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: general rules in a משנה are not absolute
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that we cannot rely on a משנה's general statement (using 'כל') as complete. This is true even when the משנה lists exceptions with 'חוץ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: We do not learn from general statements, even in a place where 'except' is said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a rule from רבי יוחנן. When a משנה says 'all' or 'anything', there may still be hidden exceptions, even if the משנה already listed some exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you might think that when a משנה says 'everything except X', everything other than X is included. רבי יוחנן says no: the listed exceptions are not necessarily the only ones. A general rule is a guideline, not a closed list.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a major rule of how to read משניות. It is quoted across ש״ס whenever someone tries to prove a הלכה from the wording of a general statement.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Yochanan said:
we do not learn from general statements,
phrases.notes: A 'כל' statement may have unstated exceptions.

phrases.english: and even in a place where 'except' is said in it.
phrases.notes: Listing some exceptions does not mean there are no others.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין לְמֵידִין מִן הַכְּלָלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא with a principle about reading the משנה's general wording ('בכל מערבין... חוץ').
steps.mimraCoreRuling: General statements in a משנה are not exhaustive, even when they explicitly list exceptions with חוץ.

steps.title: The word 'even' shows he meant a different משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that רבי יוחנן said 'even where it says חוץ'. So his main case must have been a משנה without חוץ, and not our משנה, which has חוץ. It asks which משנה that was.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he said 'even in a place where except is said', this implies he was not standing here. Where was he standing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads רבי יוחנן's words carefully and draws an inference. It then asks a question, setting up the next step, which will identify the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Even where it says חוץ' is an add-on, so his main statement must have been about a משנה with no חוץ at all. Our משנה does say חוץ ('חוץ מן המים ומן המלח'), so it can only be his secondary 'even' case. The גמרא asks which משנה was his primary target.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that he said

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as an attack on רבי יוחנן's rule. The גמרא accepts the rule and only wants to know which משנה he was originally commenting on.

phrases.english: From the fact that he said: 'even in a place'
where 'except' is said in it,
it follows that he was not standing (referring) here,
phrases.notes: Our משנה has חוץ, so it can only be the 'even' case, not the main one.

phrases.english: where was he standing?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָאָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ חוּץ, מִכְּלָל דְּלָאו הָכָא קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the precise wording of רבי יוחנן's statement in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which משנה, one without the word חוץ, was רבי יוחנן's principle primarily addressing?

steps.title: He was referring to the משנה about time-bound מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן was referring to the משנה in קידושין. That משנה says women are exempt from כל מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא and obligated in those that are not time-bound. It is a 'כל' rule with no חוץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was standing there: all positive מצוות that are time-bound, men are obligated and women are exempt. And those not time-bound, both women and men are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the source: the well-known משנה in קידושין about women and time-bound positive מצוות. This is a general 'כל' rule with no listed exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה fits perfectly: it says 'כל' and has no חוץ. So it is the main case of 'אין למדין מן הכללות'. The גמרא will next show that this rule really does have exceptions in both directions, which is why רבי יוחנן said it cannot be relied on as absolute.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in another משנה, in מסכת קידושין)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's rule 'אין למדין מן הכללות' was said mainly about the משנה of מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא. A 'כל' statement in a משנה is a guideline with possible exceptions, and that is true even when a משנה lists exceptions with חוץ.
steps.confusionAlert: The famous rule 'women are exempt from time-bound מצוות' is not a perfect law with no exceptions. That is exactly the point רבי יוחנן is making. The category stays true, but some specific מצוות turn out differently.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the foundation for the well-known exceptions to the rule of מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, which the גמרא is about to list.

phrases.english: He was standing (referring) there:
all positive commandments that are time-bound,
men are obligated and women are exempt.
And those that are not time-bound,
both women and men are obligated.
phrases.notes: A general 'כל' rule with no חוץ, the main case for רבי יוחנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 3 by identifying the משנה רבי יוחנן was referring to.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן was referring to the משנה in קידושין: 'כל מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, men are obligated and women are exempt; those not time-bound, both are obligated.' It is a general rule without חוץ.

steps.title: Time-bound מצוות that women must still do
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first half of the קידושין rule. מצה, שמחה, and הקהל are all time-bound, yet women are obligated in them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really a rule that women are exempt from every time-bound positive מצוה? There are מצה, שמחה, and הקהל. Each is a time-bound positive מצוה, and women are obligated in them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the קידושין rule and shows that its first half has exceptions. These are time-bound מצוות that women must still do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'כל', meaning 'every' time-bound מצוה exempts women. But three clear cases break that pattern. So the word 'כל' did not really mean every single case.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה to eat מצה on פסח
The מצוה to rejoice on a יום טוב
The gathering of the whole nation every seven years on סוכות to hear the תורה read

phrases.english: And is it a general rule
that for every positive מצוה caused by time
women are exempt?
But there are matza, rejoicing, and assembly,
phrases.notes: Women's obligation in each one comes from a special source in the תורה.

phrases.english: each of which is a time-bound positive מצוה,
and women are obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְלָלָא הוּא דְּכׇל מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָא נָשִׁים פְּטוּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows why the קידושין משנה from Step 4 cannot be relied on as complete.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of 'כל' in the first half of the קידושין rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Time-bound מצוות that obligate women contradict 'women are exempt from every time-bound מצוה'.

steps.title: Non-time-bound מצוות that women are exempt from
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second half of the rule. תלמוד תורה, פריה ורביה, and פדיון הבן are not time-bound, yet women are exempt from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are women really obligated in every positive מצוה that is not time-bound? There are תלמוד תורה, פריה ורביה, and פדיון הבן. None of them is time-bound, and women are exempt from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows that the second half of the קידושין rule also has exceptions. These cases break the rule in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women should be obligated in every מצוה that is not time-bound, but these three exempt them. So the rule fails in both directions. That makes it clear that a 'כל' statement is only a general guideline.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁלֹּא הַזְּמַן גְּרָמָא
phrases.english: And every positive מצוה that is not caused by time
women are obligated?
But there is Torah study,
being fruitful and multiplying, and redeeming the firstborn son,
which are positive מצוות not caused by time
and women are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁלֹּא הַזְּמַן גְּרָמָא נָשִׁים חַיָּיבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel challenge to the second half of the same rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of 'כל' in the second half of the קידושין rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מצוות that are not time-bound but still exempt women contradict 'women are obligated in every non-time-bound מצוה'.

steps.title: That is why רבי יוחנן said we cannot learn from general rules
steps.stepSummary: Because of these exceptions, רבי יוחנן said we cannot rely on general rules, even where the משנה says חוץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said: we do not learn from general rules, even in a place where it says 'except'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ties the exceptions back to רבי יוחנן's statement. This is the source that led him to say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קידושין משנה uses 'כל' without any חוץ, and it still has many exceptions. רבי יוחנן extends the lesson further. Even a list that names its own exceptions with חוץ may still be leaving some out.

keyTerms.meaning: We cannot rely on general rules to decide every case

steps.whatToRemember: A 'כל' rule in a משנה is a general guideline, not a complete list. This is true even when the משנה adds 'חוץ'.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan said:
We do not learn from general rules
even in a place where 'except' is said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the exceptions in Steps 5-6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: General 'כל' rules have unlisted exceptions, even when the rule says חוץ.

steps.title: A proof from a משנה about a זב that uses חוץ
steps.stepSummary: אביי (or רבי ירמיה) brings a משנה with a 'כל' rule about a זב that lists exceptions with חוץ. He will use it to support רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said (some say רבי ירמיה said): We also learned this in a משנה. They stated another rule. Anything carried on top of a זב is impure. Anything that a זב is carried on is pure, except for something fit for lying or sitting on, and a person.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sets up a proof that רבי יוחנן is right even about rules that say חוץ. Here he only quotes the משנה. The actual proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we only saw a rule with no חוץ. This משנה does say חוץ and names exact exceptions: bedding, seats, and a person. If something else is also missing from this list, then even חוץ lists are not complete.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who became impure through a certain bodily discharge
Something a זב lies on, which becomes impure
Something a זב sits on, which becomes impure
We too learned it, meaning there is a support from a משנה

phrases.english: Abaye said, and some say Rabbi Yirmeya:
We too have also learned it,
They stated yet another rule:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁנִּישָּׂא עַל גַּבֵּי הַזָּב — טָמֵא,
phrases.english: Anything carried on top of a zav is impure,
and anything that the zav is carried on is pure,
except for what is fit for lying and sitting on,
and a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source, a 'כל' rule with חוץ, to support the 'even with חוץ' part of רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that even a rule with חוץ is not complete
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about what is carried on a זב (Zavim 5:2)

steps.title: The list leaves out the מרכב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the זב list says חוץ, yet it does not mention מרכב, a riding item that also becomes impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there nothing else? But there is a riding item!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the core of אביי's proof. The חוץ list in the משנה misses a case the תורה itself mentions: the riding item (מרכב).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says that a מרכב a זב rides on becomes impure. The משנה's list of exceptions does not include it. If that is true, the חוץ list is incomplete.

keyTerms.meaning: A riding item, something a person rides on

phrases.english: And is there nothing else?
But there is a riding item!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finds the missing exception that makes אביי's proof work.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the חוץ list in the זב משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מרכב also becomes impure when a זב is carried on it, yet it is not listed among the exceptions.

steps.title: Is a riding item really different from a seat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a מרכב actually is. If the זב sits on it, it is already included under מושב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case of a riding item are we talking about? If he sits on it, that is just a seat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the proof. Maybe מרכב is not missing at all, because it is already covered by 'seat'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every riding item is something you sit on, then the משנה's word מושב already includes it. In that case nothing is missing from the list and the proof would fall apart. So the גמרא must find a riding item that is not a seat.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: A riding item, what is the case?
If he sits on it, that is a seat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the exception raised in Step 9 is really separate from the listed מושב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of מרכב is not already a מושב?

steps.title: The front handle of a saddle is a riding item, not a seat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that it means the front handle of the saddle (תפוס). A ברייתא teaches that this handle is impure as a מרכב, not as a מושב.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we meant: there is the upper part of the saddle. As a ברייתא teaches: the saddle is impure as a seat, and the handle is impure as a riding item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a riding item that is not a seat. This saves אביי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rider does not sit on the handle. He holds it. So it is a separate category, called מרכב, and its impurity is less severe than that of a מושב. Since the משנה's list does not include it, the חוץ list really is incomplete.

keyTerms.meaning: The handle at the front of the saddle that a rider holds
As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the saddle and the handle are the same. The saddle seat itself is a מושב. Only the handle is a separate מרכב.

phrases.english: This is what we are saying:
there is the upper part of the saddle,
as it was taught:
The saddle is impure as a seat,
and the handle is impure as a riding item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 10 by identifying a riding item that is not a seat.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תפוס of a saddle is a מרכב separate from מושב, so it is truly missing from the משנה's list.

steps.title: Proof confirmed: even a חוץ list is not complete
steps.stepSummary: Since the זב משנה leaves out the מרכב despite saying חוץ, the proof stands: we cannot learn from general rules, even where it says חוץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: we do not learn from general rules, even in a place where it says 'except'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes אביי's proof. It shows that רבי יוחנן's rule is also supported by a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זב משנה listed its exceptions with חוץ and still missed the מרכב. This proves the stronger part of רבי יוחנן's rule. Even naming exceptions does not make a list complete.
steps.whatToRemember: Both the קידושין משנה (no חוץ) and the זב משנה (with חוץ) have missing exceptions. So no 'כל' rule can be fully relied on.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is used all over ש״ס. A 'כל' in a משנה never automatically rules out other exceptions.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
we do not learn from general rules
even in a place where 'except' is said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the proof now that the מרכב is shown to be a real, missing exception.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A משנה's 'כל' rule may have unlisted exceptions, even when it explicitly lists some with חוץ.

steps.title: A second proof from our own משנה about עירוב
steps.stepSummary: רבינא (or רב נחמן) says our משנה also supports רבי יוחנן. It says you can make an עירוב or שיתוף with any food except water and salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said (some say it was רב נחמן): We also learned this in our משנה: 'You may make an עירוב and a שיתוף with anything, except water and salt.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא brings another source to back up רבי יוחנן's rule. Here he only quotes the source. The challenge that turns it into a proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is built just like the זב proof in steps 8–12. First, quote a source that says 'everything' and then lists exceptions with חוץ. Then show that something left off the list also follows the exception.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another version of who said it)
We too have learned it (in our own משנה)
One may make a שיתוף מבואות (joining an alleyway)
Except: the word that lists the exceptions

phrases.english: Ravina said, and some say it was Rav Nachman:
We too have also learned it:
With anything one may make an eruv and a shituf,
phrases.notes: This is the opening of our משנה on 26b.

phrases.english: except for water and salt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the זב proof is finished, a second, separate proof for the same rule begins.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule: אין למדין מן הכללות ואפילו במקום שנאמר בו חוץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: בכל מערבין ומשתתפין חוץ מן המים והמלח

steps.title: Truffles and mushrooms are missing from the list
steps.stepSummary: The list of exceptions seems incomplete. כמהין ופטריות also cannot be used for an עירוב, yet the משנה does not mention them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there nothing else that is excluded? But truffles and mushrooms are also excluded!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to a hole in the משנה's list. Something that should be an exception is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Truffles and mushrooms are not counted as real food (מזון), so they cannot be used for an עירוב, just like water and salt. If the list with חוץ were complete, they should have been named. This hole is what makes the proof work.

keyTerms.meaning: And is there nothing more? (Is the list really complete?)

phrases.english: And is there nothing else?
But there are truffles and mushrooms!
phrases.notes: These are not considered real food, so they cannot be used for an עירוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the list just quoted is not complete.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the משנה's list of exceptions is complete
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Truffles and mushrooms also cannot be used, yet they are not listed after חוץ.

steps.title: Conclusion: general rules are not complete, even with an exceptions list
steps.stepSummary: Since the משנה leaves out כמהין ופטריות, it is clear that general rules cannot be relied on, even when they say חוץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: we do not learn from general rules, even where the word 'except' is used.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the second proof. The missing truffles and mushrooms show that רבי יוחנן's rule is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think that once a משנה lists exceptions, it has listed all of them. This case shows that even a list with חוץ can leave things out. So a general rule in a משנה cannot be applied blindly to every case.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two proofs for רבי יוחנן: the זב list (missing the מרכב) and the עירוב list (missing truffles and mushrooms). Both show that a general rule with חוץ may still be incomplete.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key rule for how to read a משנה: a 'כל' statement is not a complete list. It shows up in other places in ש״ס as well, for example קידושין לד.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
we do not learn from general rules
even in a place where it says 'except'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the hole found in step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's rule is proven from our משנה: general rules are not complete, even when they say חוץ.

steps.title: Two Amoraim: where the teaching about water and salt belongs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה (buying food with מעשר שני money). It then says that רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי בר חנינא share one teaching, but each attaches it to a different law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Everything may be bought with מעשר money, etc.' רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי בר חנינא: one teaches it about עירוב, and one teaches it about מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It sets up a teaching that two אמוראים place in different spots. The next two steps explain each version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full line of the משנה says everything may be bought with מעשר שני money except water and salt. So both עירוב and מעשר שני share the same exception. The question is which of the two laws the coming teaching was said about.

keyTerms.meaning: מעשר שני money, which may only be spent on food to eat in ירושלים
Etc. (the rest of the quote is understood)

phrases.english: 'Everything may be bought with maaser money, etc.'
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: except for water and salt.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina:
one teaches it about eruv
and one teaches it about maaser.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two laws. עירוב is about which foods can be used to make the עירוב. מעשר שני is about what you may buy with the money. The משנה excludes water and salt from both.
steps.triggerLanguage: חַד מַתְנֵי אַעֵירוּב וְחַד מַתְנֵי אַמַּעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the חוץ discussion and starts on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two אמוראים each place one shared teaching on a different law: one on עירוב, one on מעשר שני.

steps.title: The eruv version: water and salt together are allowed
steps.stepSummary: According to the one who puts it on עירוב, water alone or salt alone is not allowed. Water and salt mixed together may be used for an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: One teaches it about עירוב: The משנה only meant water by itself or salt by itself, which cannot be used for an עירוב. But with water and salt together, one may make an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the first version. It limits the משנה's ban on water and salt when it comes to עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water or salt alone is not food, so it cannot serve as an עירוב. Mixed together, they make salty brine, which can be used as food. So the ban covers only each one separately.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught (this law is limited to a certain case)

phrases.english: One teaches it about eruv:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מַיִם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
phrases.english: They only taught it about water by itself
and salt by itself, that one may not make an eruv with them.
But with water and salt together, one may make an eruv.
phrases.notes: The mixture (brine) counts as something that can be eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד מַתְנֵי אַעֵירוּב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the two versions named in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For עירוב, water alone or salt alone is not allowed, but water and salt together are allowed.

steps.title: The maaser version: water and salt together may be bought
steps.stepSummary: According to the one who puts it on מעשר שני, water alone or salt alone may not be bought with מעשר money. Water and salt mixed together may be bought.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one teaches it about מעשר: The משנה only meant water by itself or salt by itself, which may not be bought. But water and salt together may be bought with מעשר money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the second version. It uses the same limit, but applies it to buying with מעשר שני money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording matches step 17 exactly. Only the law changes: from 'making an עירוב' to 'buying with מעשר שני money.' Once mixed, water and salt count as food that may be bought with this money.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions say the same thing: water alone or salt alone is excluded, but a water-and-salt mixture is allowed. The only question is whether this was taught about עירוב or about מעשר שני.

phrases.english: And one teaches it about maaser:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מַיִם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
phrases.english: They only taught it about water by itself
and salt by itself, that they may not be bought.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מַיִם וּמֶלַח — נִיקָּחִין בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: But water and salt together may be bought with maaser money.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד מַתְנֵי אַמַּעֲשֵׂר: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second version, a parallel to step 17, applied to מעשר שני instead of עירוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For מעשר שני, water alone or salt alone may not be bought, but water and salt together may be bought.

steps.title: How the two versions relate to each other
steps.stepSummary: The version that permits water-and-salt for מעשר שני would surely permit it for עירוב. The version that permits it for עירוב does not permit it for מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever teaches this rule about מעשר would certainly apply it to עירוב. But whoever teaches it about עירוב applies it only to עירוב, and not to מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two versions of the shared teaching from Step 16. It shows that one version is stricter than the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני is the stricter case for water-and-salt. So if the mixture is allowed there, it is obviously allowed for the easier case of עירוב (a כל שכן). The opposite does not follow: allowing it for עירוב says nothing about מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: second tithe, whose money may only buy food in ירושלים
food set down to allow carrying or walking on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the two versions are just swapping places. The מעשר version includes the עירוב law, but the עירוב version leaves out the מעשר law.

phrases.english: The one who teaches it on the second tithe,
all the more so on an eiruv.
phrases.notes: If the mixture is allowed for the stricter case, it is allowed for the easier one.

phrases.english: And the one who teaches it on an eiruv,
but on the tithe — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי אַמַּעֲשֵׂר, כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן אַעֵירוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two versions laid out in Steps 17 and 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מעשר version also allows the mixture for עירוב. The עירוב version does not allow it for מעשר.

steps.title: Why is מעשר שני stricter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the עירוב version would not allow water-and-salt for מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the difference it just described. This sets up the short answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is aimed at the second half of Step 19. Why should a mixture that is good enough for עירוב not be good enough for מעשר שני?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the distinction in Step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the mixture fails for מעשר שני even if it works for עירוב.

steps.title: מעשר שני requires real produce
steps.stepSummary: Food bought with מעשר שני money must be produce. Water and salt, even mixed together, are not produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: We require produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: מעשר שני money may only buy produce, and water-and-salt is not produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עירוב only needs something that counts as food. מעשר שני has an extra requirement: the item must be פירא, produce of the ground. Mixing water and salt makes them a usable food, but it does not turn them into produce.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the source of the strictness. It is also the background for the challenge against רבי יצחק that follows.

phrases.english: We require produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מעשר שני money may only buy produce, and water-and-salt is not produce.

steps.title: רבי יצחק teaches the version about מעשר
steps.stepSummary: When רבי יצחק came to Bavel, he taught the teaching as applying to מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יצחק came from ארץ ישראל, he taught this rule about the second tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רבי יצחק held the broader version: water-and-salt may even be bought with מעשר שני money. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק chose the version that goes against the 'we require produce' reasoning of Step 21. That makes his version the natural target for an objection.

keyTerms.meaning: when (someone) came from ארץ ישראל to Bavel

phrases.english: When Rabbi Yitzchak came,
he taught it on the second tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַבִּי יִצְחָק, מַתְנֵי אַמַּעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks one of the two versions as authoritative.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water and salt mixed together may be bought with מעשר שני money.

steps.title: The testimony about buying fish brine with מעשר money
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted. רבי יהודה בן גדיש testified that his family bought fish brine with מעשר money. רבי אליעזר limited this to brine with fish innards mixed in.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him from a ברייתא. רבי יהודה בן גדיש testified before רבי אליעזר: 'My father's household used to buy fish brine with מעשר money.' רבי אליעזר answered: 'Perhaps you only heard this when fish innards were mixed into the brine.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבי יצחק. This step lays out the story, and the next step makes the challenge sharp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Brine is basically salty water. רבי אליעזר would not allow even brine unless real pieces of fish were mixed in. That suggests salty liquid alone cannot be bought with מעשר money.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi Yehuda ben Gadish testified
before Rabbi Eliezer:
My father's household used to buy
fish brine with tithe money.
He said to him: Perhaps you only heard it
when fish innards
were mixed into it.
phrases.notes: The real fish in the mixture is what makes it qualify.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן גָּדִישׁ לִפְנֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source against רבי יצחק's version.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's version that water-and-salt may be bought with מעשר money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר required real fish even in brine, so salty liquid alone is not enough.

steps.title: Even the lenient view was only about brine
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי יהודה בן גדיש allowed only brine, because it contains fat from food. Plain water and salt would not be allowed. רב יוסף is introduced to respond.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even רבי יהודה בן גדיש spoke only about brine, because it is the fat of produce. But water and salt — no. רב יוסף said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge: no one in the ברייתא allows plain water and salt for מעשר money. That contradicts רבי יצחק. The last words introduce רב יוסף, whose answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two opinions in the ברייתא, and both are stricter than רבי יצחק. רבי יהודה בן גדיש allowed brine only because fish fat dissolves into it. Water and salt have no food content at all.

keyTerms.meaning: the fat of produce (here, fish fat in the brine)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא suggests water-and-salt alone may not be bought with מעשר money, which is a problem for רבי יצחק. רב יוסף is about to answer.

phrases.english: And even Rabbi Yehuda ben Gadish
only said it about brine,
which is the fat of produce,
but water and salt — no.
Rav Yosef said:
phrases.notes: This introduces the answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן גָּדִישׁ לָא קָאָמַר אֶלָּא בְּצִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא that completes the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's version that permits water-and-salt for מעשר שני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both opinions in the ברייתא require some real food content. Plain water-and-salt has none, so it may not be bought with מעשר money.
